newsitem.title: USA: Pact signed with potential bidders - Big B.
newsitem.headline: Pact signed with potential bidders - Big B.

text.p: Big B said on Wednesday that it has signed confidentiality agreements with a number of other potentially interested parties.
In a letter to Revco D.S. Inc, Anthony Bruno, Big B chairman and chief executive officer, also wrote to encourage Revco to "execute a confidentiality agreement on terms Big B can accept."
The letter addressed to Dwayne Hoven, Revco's president and chief executive officer was disclosed in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

In the October 1 letter, Bruno wrote that "provided a suitable agreement can be reached, I and other members of the Big B Board of Directors would welcome Revco's active participation in the process."

Revco previously had said it wants to sign a cofidentiality pact, but objected to certain provisions of Big B's proposed agreement. It also filed suit late last month in U.S. district court seeking to block an anti-takeover plan enacted by Big B.
Bruno wrote Hoven that "no party other than Revco has advised Big B that it will not execute a confidentiality agreement" because of certain provisions.

Although the other parties did not object to the terms, Big B still wants to reach a mutally acceptable pact with Revco and sent them revised provisions which Bruno said "appropriately balances Big B's and Revco's interests."
Big B also said Revco's suit questioning its poison bill anti-takeover plan "is clearly premature and "inimical" to Big B's developing other alternative proposals.
Big B said it contacted the other parties that had already signed confidentiality pacts of its offer to revise their agreements in accordance with the revised confidentiality agreement.

In the filing, Big B said on October 1, it filed a motion to remand the Rights Plan Litigation to the circuit court of Jefferson County, Alabama. It said it filed the motion because of an action by Revco to remove the litigation from the circuit court.
